title: Blueberries vs. strawberries: fiber, sugar and micronutrients

seo.title: Blueberries vs. strawberries: fiber, sugar and vitamins
seo.meta_description: Per 100 g, blueberries provide 57 calories, 10 g sugar and 2.4 g fiber; strawberries provide 32 calories, 4.9 g sugar and 2 g fiber. Compare vitamin C and K too.
seo.search_intent: Compare blueberries and strawberries for fiber, sugar, calories and micronutrients

excerpt: Blueberries and strawberries are both low-energy whole fruits, but they are not identical. Per 100 g, blueberries provide about 57 calories, 10 g sugar and 2.4 g fiber; strawberries provide 32 calories, 4.9 g sugar and 2 g fiber. Strawberries contain about six times as much vitamin C, while blueberries provide more vitamin K in USDA reference data.
content_html:
Blueberries and strawberries often share the same yogurt bowl, smoothie and antioxidant list. Their overall nutrition profiles are more alike than different, but strawberries contain substantially less sugar and much more vitamin C for the same weight.

Compare 100 g with 100 g

Per 100 gBlueberriesStrawberries
Calories5732
Sugars10.0 g4.9 g
Fiber2.4 g2.0 g
Protein0.7 g0.7 g
Vitamin C9.7 mg58.8 mg
Folate6 mcg24 mcg
Vitamin K19.3 mcg2.2 mcg

The fiber difference is small—only 0.4 g per 100 g. The large differences are vitamin C, sugar and calorie density.

What does a 150 g bowl look like?

At 150 g, blueberries provide about 86 calories, 15 g sugar and 3.6 g fiber. Strawberries provide about 48 calories, 7.3 g sugar and 3.0 g fiber.

The strawberry portion also supplies about 88 mg vitamin C, versus roughly 15 mg from the blueberries.

Does that make strawberries better?

If your specific comparison is vitamin C or lower calorie density, strawberries clearly lead. If the target is vitamin K, the USDA blueberry reference is higher.

But turning every nutrient into a winner-take-all contest misses the larger point: both are whole fruits with water, fiber and different mixtures of phytochemicals.

The pigments differ too

Blueberries contain a broad mixture of anthocyanins responsible for their blue-purple color. Strawberries also contain anthocyanins, with pelargonidin derivatives prominent in their red color.

Darker color is not a universal health score. Cultivar, ripeness, storage and analytical method all affect measured polyphenols.

Fresh or frozen both work

Unsweetened frozen berries are a practical alternative when fresh fruit is expensive or out of season. Jam and sweetened berry products are a different comparison because added sugar raises the energy and sugar concentration.

There is no need to crown one global winner between fresh blueberries and strawberries. Rotating both gives you different nutrient and phytochemical profiles.

faq.question: Which has more sugar, blueberries or strawberries?
faq.answer: Blueberries: about 10 g/100 g versus 4.9 g/100 g in strawberries in the USDA references used here.

faq.question: Which has more fiber?
faq.answer: Blueberries slightly: 2.4 g versus 2.0 g per 100 g. The difference is small.

faq.question: Which has more vitamin C?
faq.answer: Strawberries by a wide margin: 58.8 mg/100 g versus 9.7 mg in blueberries.

faq.question: Are frozen berries still a good choice?
faq.answer: Yes. Unsweetened frozen whole berries retain much of their nutrition and can be a practical year-round option.
